content.topic: Seek to understand others, and you will be understood

modelEssay.title: Seek to Understand Others, and You Will Be Understood
modelEssay.content:
The adage 'Seek to understand others, and you will be understood' profoundly resonates with the essence of human interaction. It underscores the importance of empathy and mutual comprehension in fostering strong relationships.

In our daily lives, this principle manifests in various ways. For instance, when engaging in a conversation, actively listening to the other person's perspective not only shows respect but also encourages them to reciprocate. This two-way understanding can lead to more productive discussions and stronger bonds. Moreover, in the workplace, seeking to understand colleagues' ideas and challenges can lead to better collaboration and a more harmonious environment.

In conclusion, the wisdom of this saying is undeniable. By striving to understand others, we open ourselves to being understood, which is the cornerstone of effective communication and meaningful connections.

transcript.text: You're going to give a short speech of thanks for the speaker this evening, aren't you, Bill?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 比尔，你今晚要为演讲者做简短的感谢致辞，对吧？

transcript.text: Yes.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 是的。

transcript.speaker: F

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 不，我真的不介意，但我永远忘不了我第一次做的感谢致辞。

transcript.text: Why, what happened?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 为什么，发生了什么？

transcript.text: Well, I was in my early twenties.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 嗯，我那时二十出头。

transcript.text: I had joined the local history society.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我加入了当地的历史学会。

transcript.text: Yes.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 是的。

transcript.text: Anyway, I went along to a lecture by a Miss Bly.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 总之，我去听了布莱小姐的一个讲座。

transcript.text: Oh, do go on.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 哦，请继续说。

transcript.text: She was going to talk, with slides, about our town in the 18th century.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 她打算用幻灯片讲述我们镇在18世纪的历史。

transcript.text: She had just published a book on the subject, which was reckoned to be quite good.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 她刚刚出版了一本关于这个主题的书，被认为相当不错。

transcript.text: So, I went along.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 所以，我就去了。

transcript.text: When I arrived, the secretary asked me if I could give the speech of thanks.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我到达时，秘书问我是否可以做感谢致辞。

transcript.text: Rather stupidly, I said yes.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我相当愚蠢地答应了。

transcript.text: We've all done it.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我们都做过这样的事。

transcript.text: Anyway, from that point on, I was scared.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 总之，从那一刻起，我害怕了。

transcript.text: What should I say?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我该说什么呢？

transcript.text: I decided to make notes during the lecture and refer to interesting parts and thank her on behalf of the society.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我决定在讲座期间做笔记，提到有趣的部分，并代表学会感谢她。

transcript.text: In fact, by the time Miss Bly stood up to talk, I was feeling much better.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 事实上，到布莱小姐站起来讲话时，我感觉好多了。

transcript.text: But she was so nervous that she kept forgetting what to say.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 但她太紧张了，总是忘记该说什么。

transcript.text: And she spoke almost in a whisper.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 而且她说话几乎像耳语一样。

transcript.text: People at the back kept calling out, we can't hear.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 后排的人不断喊道，我们听不见。

transcript.text: It was embarrassing.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 真尴尬。

transcript.text: I can imagine it.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我能想象。

transcript.text: At least the slides were good.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 至少幻灯片很好。

transcript.text: That is, until the bulb in the projector blew, and she had to finish the talk with no illustrations.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 也就是说，直到投影仪的灯泡烧了，她不得不在没有插图的情况下结束讲座。

transcript.text: So what did you say in your speech of thanks?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 那么你在感谢致辞中说了什么？

transcript.text: What can you say?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你能说什么呢？

transcript.text: You have to be polite.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你必须礼貌点。

transcript.text: I mentioned the interesting facts, referred to the excellent slides, and then finished up by saying, we'd all like to thank Miss Bly for blowing us her slides.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我提到了有趣的事实，提到了精彩的幻灯片，最后说，我们都感谢布莱小姐为我们吹灭了她的幻灯片。

transcript.text: Oh no!
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 哦，不！

transcript.text: I felt terrible.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我感觉糟透了。

transcript.text: I tried to apologize, not very successfully.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我试图道歉，但不太成功。

transcript.text: And the speech of thanks this evening?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 那么今晚的感谢致辞呢？

transcript.text: I'll write down exactly what I'm going to say, and read it carefully.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我会把我要说的话一字不差地写下来，然后仔细阅读。

transcript.text: This report corresponds with the existing scientific literature on bedtime and wellness.
transcript.translation: 这份报告与现有的关于就寝时间和健康的科学文献相符。

transcript.text: The relationship between getting more sleep and making better food choices is well documented.
transcript.translation: 获得更多睡眠与做出更好食物选择之间的关系有充分记录。

transcript.text: A study published last year in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition found that people who sleep more tend to eat less unhealthy food than their peers who don't get as much rest.
transcript.translation: 去年发表在《美国临床营养学杂志》上的一项研究发现，睡眠更多的人往往比休息不足的同龄人吃更少的不健康食品。

transcript.translation: 加州大学伯克利分校2015年的一项研究发现，晚睡的青少年在五年期间更有可能体重增加。

transcript.translation: 一个人睡得越晚，第二天记录的卡路里就越多。

transcript.text: Still, if late sleepers want to lose a few pounds, they can go to bed earlier than they usually do, thereby reducing their chances of taking snacks before bedtime.
transcript.translation: 尽管如此，如果晚睡者想减掉几磅，他们可以比通常更早睡觉，从而减少睡前吃零食的机会。

transcript.text: When purchasing life insurance, there are many important factors to consider.
transcript.translation: 在购买人寿保险时，有许多重要因素需要考虑。

transcript.text: One should buy the policies that give the most protection at the least cost, insure the right family members and consider the family's financial needs.
transcript.translation: 人们应该购买那些以最低成本提供最大保障的保单，为正确的家庭成员投保，并考虑家庭的财务需求。

transcript.text: It is important to buy the insurance from companies that are financially sound and that are represented by honest, well-trained agents.
transcript.translation: 重要的是从财务状况稳健、并由诚实、训练有素的代理人代表的公司购买保险。

transcript.text: At various stages in a person's life, different kinds of life insurance are needed for particular situations.
transcript.translation: 在一个人生命的各个阶段，特定情况需要不同类型的人寿保险。

transcript.text: Jerry is single and has no dependents.
transcript.translation: Jerry是单身，没有受抚养人。

transcript.text: Probably the only life insurance he needs is enough to cover his debts and burial expenses.
transcript.translation: 他可能唯一需要的人寿保险是足以覆盖他的债务和丧葬费用的金额。

transcript.text: Insurance can be purchased at a lower rate during the young years, but by buying while young, the premiums are paid in for a longer period of time.
transcript.translation: 年轻时可以以较低的费率购买保险，但通过在年轻时购买，保费支付的时间更长。

transcript.text: In the end, the amount paid for premiums is about the same.
transcript.translation: 最终，支付的保费总额大致相同。

transcript.text: A person shouldn't buy insurance protection that really isn't necessary.
transcript.translation: 人们不应该购买那些真正不必要的保险保障。

transcript.text: Suppose that Jerry marries Jeanette, who is a college graduate and is working.
transcript.translation: 假设Jerry娶了Jeanette，她是大学毕业生且正在工作。

transcript.text: Perhaps enough insurance would be needed to cover their debts and burial expenses.
transcript.translation: 可能需要足够的保险来覆盖他们的债务和丧葬费用。

transcript.text: Now, Jeanette has quit work and their first child is on the way.
transcript.translation: 现在，Jeanette已辞职，他们的第一个孩子即将出生。

transcript.text: They have purchased a home with a small down payment and a 30-year mortgage.
transcript.translation: 他们用小额首付和30年期的抵押贷款购买了一处房产。

transcript.text: The situation regarding life insurance takes on a different look.
transcript.translation: 关于人寿保险的情况呈现出不同的面貌。

transcript.text: There are dependents who need financial protection.
transcript.translation: 有需要财务保护的受抚养人。

transcript.text: How much insurance is needed?
transcript.translation: 需要多少保险？

transcript.text: As the family increases in size, it is essential to add more insurance on the breadwinner to protect the dependents.
transcript.translation: 随着家庭规模扩大，必须为养家糊口的人增加更多保险以保护受抚养人。

transcript.text: When the children are young and depend upon the family for financial needs, families with modest incomes have difficulty providing enough life insurance to protect the mother and the children.
transcript.translation: 当孩子们年幼且依赖家庭财务需求时，收入不高的家庭难以提供足够的人寿保险来保护母亲和孩子们。

transcript.text: Families with modest incomes should insure the breadwinner or breadwinners first.
transcript.translation: 收入不高的家庭应首先为养家糊口的人投保。

transcript.text: When considering the amount of insurance for the mother with dependent children, substitute child care is a need that should be planned for until the children can care for themselves.
transcript.translation: 在为有受抚养子女的母亲考虑保险金额时，应规划替代儿童护理的需求，直到孩子们能够自理。

transcript.text: The death of a small child would have no effect upon the income of the family.
transcript.translation: 幼童的死亡不会对家庭收入产生影响。

transcript.text: Perhaps a policy to meet funeral expenses would be sufficient for the young child, although most people do not take out insurance on their young children.
transcript.translation: 或许一份满足丧葬费用的保单对幼童来说就足够了，尽管大多数人不会为他们的幼童投保。

transcript.text: As the children become financially independent of the family, the emphasis on family financial security will shift from protection to saving for the retirement years.
transcript.translation: 随着孩子们在财务上独立于家庭，家庭财务安全的重点将从保护转向为退休岁月储蓄。

transcript.text: Every family situation is different, but it is important that each family give adequate thought to planning its financial future.
transcript.translation: 每个家庭的情况都不同，但重要的是每个家庭都充分考虑其财务未来的规划。

transcript.text: Stereotype may sound like a bad word, but there's nothing bad about it.
transcript.translation: 刻板印象可能听起来像一个坏词，但它本身并没有什么不好。

transcript.text: For one thing, stereotypes are often accurate.
transcript.translation: 首先，刻板印象往往是准确的。

transcript.text: When you ask people about their concept of stereotypes, they get it pretty much right.
transcript.translation: 当你询问人们对刻板印象的概念时，他们通常理解得相当正确。

transcript.text: Also, stereotypes are often positive, particularly of groups that we ourselves belong to.
transcript.translation: 此外，刻板印象通常是积极的，尤其是关于我们自己所属的群体。

transcript.text: Some of the statistical generalisations may be positive, as some groups have reputations for being smart, for being loyal, for being brave, for all sorts of things that are not at all negative.
transcript.translation: 一些统计概括可能是积极的，因为某些群体以聪明、忠诚、勇敢等各种非负面的特质而闻名。

transcript.text: And so there's nothing inherently wrong about stereotypes.
transcript.translation: 因此，刻板印象本身并没有什么固有的错误。

transcript.text: But there are problems with stereotypes.
transcript.translation: 但刻板印象也存在问题。

transcript.text: For one thing, they are reliable insofar as they are based on unbiased samples.
transcript.translation: 首先，只要它们基于无偏见的样本，它们就是可靠的。

transcript.text: But a lot of the information we get about human groups is through biased sources, like how they are represented in the media.
transcript.translation: 但我们获得的关于人类群体的很多信息来自有偏见的来源，比如媒体中的呈现方式。

transcript.text: And if these sources don't give you an accurate depiction, your stereotype won't be accurate.
transcript.translation: 如果这些来源没有给你准确的描绘，你的刻板印象就不会准确。

transcript.text: For example, many Jews have been troubled by Shakespeare's depiction of Shylock.
transcript.translation: 例如，许多犹太人因莎士比亚对夏洛克的描绘而感到困扰。

transcript.text: If the only Jew you know is Shakespeare's Shylock, it's going to be a very bad impression.
transcript.translation: 如果你唯一认识的犹太人就是莎士比亚笔下的夏洛克，那将会是一个非常糟糕的印象。

transcript.text: So one problem with stereotypes is while we're good at drawing conclusions from them, often our information isn't reliable.
transcript.translation: 所以，刻板印象的一个问题是，虽然我们擅长从中得出结论，但我们的信息往往不可靠。

transcript.text: A second problem is that stereotypes, regardless of whether or not they're accurate, can have a negative effect on the people that they apply to.
transcript.translation: 第二个问题是，刻板印象无论是否准确，都可能对其适用对象产生负面影响。

transcript.text: And this is what psychologist Claude Steele described as stereotype threat.
transcript.translation: 这正是心理学家克劳德·斯蒂尔所描述的刻板印象威胁。

transcript.text: He has a vivid example of this.
transcript.translation: 他对此有一个生动的例子。

transcript.text: Here's how to make African Americans do worse on a math test.
transcript.translation: 以下是如何让非裔美国人在数学考试中表现更差的方法。

transcript.text: You have the test and you put on the test that they have to identify their race.
transcript.translation: 你进行考试，并在考试中要求他们标识自己的种族。

transcript.text: The very act of acknowledging that they're African American when given a test ignites in them thoughts of their own stereotype, which is negative regarding academics, and that makes them do worse.
transcript.translation: 在考试中承认自己是非裔美国人这一行为，会激发他们对自己刻板印象的联想，即对学术能力的负面看法，这导致他们表现更差。

transcript.text: Want to know how to make a woman do worse on a math test?
transcript.translation: 想知道如何让女性在数学考试中表现更差吗？

transcript.text: Same thing.
transcript.translation: 同样的方法。

transcript.text: Get her to write down her sex.
transcript.translation: 让她写下自己的性别。

transcript.text: One recent study found a sort of clever twist on this.
transcript.translation: 最近的一项研究发现了一种巧妙的转折。

transcript.text: When Asian American women are given a test and they're asked to mark down their race, they do better than they would otherwise do.
transcript.translation: 当亚裔美国女性参加考试并被要求标注自己的种族时，她们的表现比平时更好。

transcript.text: They're reminded of a positive stereotype that boosts their morale.
transcript.translation: 她们被提醒了一个积极的刻板印象，这提升了她们的士气。

transcript.text: You ask them, on the other hand, to mark down their sex, they do worse because they're reminded of a negative stereotype.
transcript.translation: 另一方面，如果你要求她们标注自己的性别，她们表现更差，因为她们被提醒了一个负面的刻板印象。

transcript.text: That's an example of how stereotypes have a potentially damaging effect on people.
transcript.translation: 这是一个刻板印象如何对人们产生潜在破坏性影响的例子。

transcript.text: Sometimes, when you take a common drug, you may have a side effect.
transcript.translation: 有时，服用常见药物可能会产生副作用。

transcript.text: That is, the drug may cause some effect other than its intended one.

transcript.text: When these side effects occur, they are called adverse reactions.
transcript.translation: 当这些副作用发生时，它们被称为不良反应。

transcript.text: Whenever you have an adverse reaction, you should stop taking the drug right away.
transcript.translation: 一旦出现不良反应，应立即停止服用该药物。

transcript.text: Ask your pharmacist whether he can suggest a drug that will relieve the symptoms, but that will not cause the adverse reaction.

transcript.text: If an adverse reaction to a drug is serious, consult your doctor for advice at once.
transcript.translation: 如果对药物的不良反应严重，应立即咨询医生的意见。

transcript.text: Drugs that are safe in the dosage stated on the label may be very dangerous in large doses.
transcript.translation: 在标签上注明的剂量内安全的药物，如果大量服用可能非常危险。

transcript.text: For example, aspirin is seldom thought of as dangerous, but there are many reports of accidental poisoning of young children who take too many aspirin pills, as well as the possible development of Reye's syndrome in children with the flu.
transcript.translation: 例如，阿司匹林很少被认为危险，但有许多关于幼童因服用过多阿司匹林药片而意外中毒的报告，以及流感儿童可能发展出Reye综合征的报道。

transcript.text: In adults, excessive use of some pain-killing drugs may cause severe kidney damage.
transcript.translation: 在成年人中，过度使用某些止痛药可能导致严重的肾脏损伤。

transcript.text: Some drugs for relief of stomach upsets, when taken in excess, can perhaps cause serious digestive problems.
transcript.translation: 一些用于缓解胃部不适的药物，如果过量服用，可能会导致严重的消化问题。

transcript.text: You should never use any over-the-counter drug on a regular, continued basis or in large quantities, except on your doctor's advice.
transcript.translation: 除非得到医生的建议，否则不应常规、持续使用任何非处方药，或大量服用。

transcript.text: You could be suffering from a serious illness that needs a doctor's care.
transcript.translation: 你可能正患有需要医生治疗的严重疾病。

transcript.text: Each drug you take not only acts on the body, but may also alter the effect of any other drug you are taking.
transcript.translation: 你服用的每种药物不仅作用于身体，还可能改变你正在服用的任何其他药物的效果。

transcript.text: Sometimes this can cause dangerous or even fatal reactions.
transcript.translation: 有时这可能导致危险甚至致命的反应。

transcript.text: For example, aspirin increases the blood-thinning effects of drugs given to patients with heart disease.
transcript.translation: 例如，阿司匹林会增强给心脏病患者的药物的血液稀释效果。

transcript.text: Therefore, a patient who has been taking such a drug may risk bleeding if he or she uses aspirin for a headache.
transcript.translation: 因此，正在服用此类药物的患者，如果为头痛使用阿司匹林，可能会面临出血风险。

transcript.text: Before using several drugs together, you should ask your doctor and follow his advice.
transcript.translation: 在同时使用多种药物之前，应咨询医生并遵循其建议。

transcript.text: Your pharmacist can tell you whether certain drugs can safely be taken together.
transcript.translation: 药剂师可以告诉你某些药物是否可以安全地一起服用。

transcript.text: Alcohol may increase the effect of a drug.
transcript.translation: 酒精可能会增强药物的效果。

transcript.text: Sleeping pills combine with alcohol to produce a sleepy feeling.
transcript.translation: 安眠药与酒精结合会产生昏睡感。

transcript.text: When taking any drug, you should ask your doctor whether drinking alcohol could be dangerous in combination with the medicine.
transcript.translation: 服用任何药物时，应询问医生饮酒是否可能与药物产生危险的相互作用。

transcript.text: Experts believe there is a relationship between adult abuse of legitimate medicines and the drug culture that has swept our country.
transcript.translation: 专家认为，成年人滥用合法药物与席卷全国的药物文化之间存在联系。

transcript.text: You can do your share to reduce the chances that your children will become part of the drug culture by treating all medicines with respect.
transcript.translation: 通过尊重对待所有药物，你可以尽自己的一份力，减少孩子成为药物文化一部分的可能性。

transcript.text: Always let your children know that medicines and drugs should not be used carelessly.
transcript.translation: 务必让孩子知道，药物不应被随意使用。

questionGroups.title: Data sharing: An open mind on open data

material.title: Data sharing: An open mind on open data

paragraphs.text: It is a movement building steady momentum: a call to make research data, software code and experimental methods publicly available and transparent. A spirit of openness is gaining acceptance in the science community, and is the only way, say advocates, to address a 'crisis' in science whereby too few findings are successfully reproduced. Furthermore, they say, it is the best way for researchers to gather the range of observations that are necessary to speed up discoveries or to identify large-scale trends.
paragraphs.translation: 这是一个势头稳步增强的运动：呼吁公开和透明地提供研究数据、软件代码和实验方法。开放精神在科学界正获得认可，倡导者称这是解决科学“危机”的唯一途径，该危机表现为成功复制的发现太少。此外，他们说，这是研究人员收集加速发现或识别大规模趋势所需观测范围的最佳方式。

paragraphs.text: The open-data shift poses a confusing problem for junior researchers. On the one hand, the drive to share is gathering official steam. Since 2013, global scientific bodies have begun to back politics that support increased public access to research. On the other hand, scientists disagree about how much and when they should share data, and they debate whether sharing it is more likely to accelerate science and make it more robust, or to introduce vulnerabilities and problems. As more journals and funders adopt data-sharing requirements, and as a growing number of enthusiasts call for more openness, junior researchers must find their place between adopters and those who continue to hold out, even as they strive to launch their own careers.
paragraphs.translation: 开放数据转变给初级研究人员带来了一个令人困惑的问题。一方面，分享的动力正在获得官方支持。自2013年以来，全球科学机构开始支持增加公众获取研究机会的政策。另一方面，科学家对分享多少数据和何时分享存在分歧，他们争论分享数据是否更可能加速科学并使其更强大，还是会引入漏洞和问题。随着更多期刊和资助者采用数据共享要求，以及越来越多的爱好者呼吁更多开放性，初级研究人员必须在采纳者和坚持者之间找到自己的位置，同时努力开创自己的职业生涯。

paragraphs.text: One key challenge facing young scientists is how to be open without becoming scientifically vulnerable. They must determine the risk of jeopardizing a job offer or a collaboration proposal from those who are wary of-or unfamiliar with-open science. And they must learn how to capitalize on the movement's benefits, such as opportunities for more citations and a way to build a reputation without the need for conventional metrics, such as publication in high-impact journals.
paragraphs.translation: 年轻科学家面临的一个关键挑战是如何在保持开放的同时避免科学上的脆弱。他们必须评估那些对开放科学持谨慎态度或不熟悉的人可能危及工作机会或合作提案的风险。此外，他们必须学会如何利用该运动的好处，例如获得更多引用的机会，以及在无需传统指标（如在高影响力期刊上发表论文）的情况下建立声誉的方法。

paragraphs.text: Some fields have embraced open data more than others. Researchers in psychology, a field rocked by findings of irreproducibility in the past few years, have been especially vocal sup-porters of the drive for more-open science. A few psychology journals have created incentives to increase interest in reproducible science—for example, by affixing an 'open-data' badge to articles that clearly state where data are available. According to social psychologist Brian Nosek, executive director of the Center for Open Science, the average data-sharing rate for the journal Psychological Science, which uses the badges, increased tenfold to 38% from 2013 to 2015.
paragraphs.translation: 一些领域比其他领域更早拥抱开放数据。心理学领域的研究人员，该领域过去几年因不可复制的发现而震动，尤其积极支持推动更开放的科学。一些心理学期刊设立了激励措施以提高对可复制科学的兴趣——例如，为明确说明数据可获取位置的论文附加“开放数据”徽章。根据社会心理学家、开放科学中心执行主任Brian Nosek的说法，使用徽章的期刊《心理科学》的平均数据共享率从2013年到2015年增加了十倍，达到38%。

paragraphs.text: Funders, too, are increasingly adopting an open-data policy. Several strongly encourage, and some require, a data-management plan that makes data available. The US National Science Foundation is among these, Some philanthropic (慈善的) funders, including the Bill &Melinda Gates Foundation in Seattle, Washington, and the Wellcome Trust in London, also data mandate open data from their grant recipients.
paragraphs.translation: 资助者也越来越采用开放数据政策。一些机构强烈鼓励，有些甚至要求制定使数据可用的数据管理计划。美国国家科学基金会就是其中之一。一些慈善资助者，包括位于华盛顿州西雅图的比尔及梅琳达·盖茨基金会和伦敦的惠康基金会，也强制要求其受赠者开放数据。

paragraphs.text: But many young researchers, especially those who have not been mentored in open science, are uncertain about whether to share or to stay private. Graduate students and postdocs, who often are working on their lab head's grant, may have no choice if their supervisor or another senior opposes sharing.
paragraphs.translation: 但许多年轻研究人员，特别是那些未在开放科学方面受过指导的人，不确定是分享还是保持私有。研究生和博士后通常在其实验室负责人的资助下工作，如果他们的导师或其他资深人员反对分享，他们可能没有选择。

paragraphs.text: Some fear that the potential impact of sharing is too high, especially at the early stages of a career. "Everybody has a scary story about someone getting scooped (被抢先)," says New York University astronomer David Hogg. Those fears may be a factor in a lingering hesitation to share data even when publishing in journals that mandate it.
paragraphs.translation: 一些人担心分享的潜在影响太大，尤其是在职业生涯早期。纽约大学天文学家David Hogg说：“每个人都听过关于有人被抢先的可怕故事。”这些恐惧可能是即使在强制要求分享数据的期刊上发表论文时，仍对分享数据犹豫不决的一个因素。

paragraphs.text: Researchers at small labs or at institutions focused on teaching arguably have the most to lose when sharing hard-won data. "With my institution and teaching load, I don't have postdocs and grad students", says Terry McGlynn, a tropical biologist at California State University, Dominguez Hills. "The stakes are higher to share data because it's a bigger fraction of what's happening in my lab."
paragraphs.translation: 小实验室或以教学为主的研究机构的研究人员在分享来之不易的数据时，可以说损失最大。加州州立大学多明戈斯山分校的热带生物学家Terry McGlynn说：“在我的机构和教学负担下，我没有博士后和研究生。”“分享数据的风险更高，因为它在我的实验室中占更大比例。

paragraphs.text: Researchers also point to the time sink that is involved in preparing data for others to view. Once the data and associated materials appear in a repository (存储库), answering questions and handling complaints can take many hours.
paragraphs.translation: 研究人员还指出，为他人查看准备数据所涉及的时间投入很大。一旦数据和相关材料出现在存储库中，回答问题和处理投诉可能需要很多小时。

paragraphs.text: The time investment can present other problems. In some cases, says data scientist Karthik Ram, it may be difficult for junior researchers to embrace openness when senior colleagues— many of whom head selection and promotion committees—might ridicule what they may view as misplaced energies. "I've heard this recently -that embracing the idea of open data and code makes traditional academics uncomfortable, "says Ram. "The concern seems to be that open advocates don't spend their time being as productive as possible."
paragraphs.translation: 时间投入可能带来其他问题。数据科学家Karthik Ram说，在某些情况下，当资深同事——其中许多领导选拔和晋升委员会——可能嘲笑他们视为精力放错了地方时，初级研究人员可能难以接受开放性。Ram说：“我最近听到这种说法——拥抱开放数据和代码的想法让传统学者感到不安。”“担忧似乎是开放倡导者没有尽可能高效地利用时间。

paragraphs.text: An open-science stance can also add complexity to a collaboration. Kate Ratliff, who studies social attitudes at the University of Florida, Gainesville, says that it can seem as if there are two camps in a field-those who care about open science and those who don't. " There's a new area to navigate-'Are you cool with the fact that I'll want to make the data open?'-when talking with somebody about an interesting research idea, "she says.
paragraphs.translation: 开放科学立场也可能增加合作的复杂性。佛罗里达大学盖恩斯维尔分校研究社会态度的Kate Ratliff说，在一个领域中似乎有两个阵营——关心开放科学的和不关心的。她说：“当与某人讨论有趣的研究想法时，有一个新的领域需要探索——‘你对我想要公开数据这件事感到OK吗？’

paragraphs.text: Despite complications and concerns, the upsides of sharing can be significant. For example, when information is uploaded to a repository, a digital object identifier(DOI) is assigned. Scientists can use a DOI to publish each step of the research life cycle, not just the final paper. In so doing, they can potentially get three citations- one each for the data and software. in addition to the paper itself. And although some say that citations for software or data have little currency in academia, they can have other benefits.
paragraphs.translation: 尽管存在复杂性和担忧，但分享的好处可能很显著。例如，当信息上传到存储库时，会分配一个数字对象标识符（DOI）。科学家可以使用DOI发布研究生命周期的每一步，而不仅仅是最终论文。这样做，他们可能获得三次引用——数据和软件各一次，加上论文本身。尽管有些人说软件或数据的引用在学术界价值不大，但它们可能有其他好处。

paragraphs.text: Many advocates think that transparent data procedures with a date and time stamp will protect scientists from being scooped. "This is the sweet spot between sharing and getting credit for it. while discouraging plagiarism (剽窃). " says Ivo Grigorov, a project coordinator at the National Institute of Aquatic Resources Research Secretariat in Charlottenlund, Denmark. Hogg says that scooping is less of a problem than many think. "The two cases I'm familiar with didn't involve open data or code, "he says.
paragraphs.translation: 许多倡导者认为，带有日期和时间戳的透明数据程序将保护科学家免遭抢先。丹麦夏洛滕隆国家水产资源研究秘书处的项目协调员Ivo Grigorov说：“这是在分享和获得认可之间取得平衡，同时阻止剽窃。”Hogg说，抢先问题没有许多人想的那么严重。他说：“我熟悉的两个案例不涉及开放数据或代码。

paragraphs.text: Open science also offers junior researchers the chance to level the playing field by gaining better access to crucial data. Ross Mounce, a postdoc studying evolutionary biology at the University of Cambridge, UK, is a vocal champion of open science, partly because of his fossil based research on access to others' data. He says that more openness in science could help to discourage what some perceive as a common practice of shutting out early-career scientists' requests for data.
paragraphs.translation: 开放科学还为初级研究人员提供了通过更好获取关键数据来平衡竞争环境的机会。英国剑桥大学研究进化生物学的博士后Ross Mounce是开放科学的积极倡导者，部分原因是他基于化石的研究需要访问他人的数据。他说，科学中更多的开放性可能有助于阻止一些人认为的排斥早期职业科学家数据请求的常见做法。

paragraphs.text: Communication also helps for those who worry about jeopardizing a collaboration, he says, Concerns about open science should be discussed at the outset of a study. "Whenever you start a project with someone, you have to establish a clear understanding of expectations for who owns the data, at what point they go public and who can do what with them," he says.
paragraphs.translation: 他说，沟通也有助于那些担心危及合作的人，关于开放科学的担忧应该在研究开始时讨论。他说：“每当你与某人开始一个项目时，你必须就数据所有权、何时公开以及谁可以对数据做什么等期望达成明确共识。”

paragraphs.text: In the end, sharing data, software and materials with colleagues can help an early -career researcher to gain recognition--a crucial component of success. "The thing you are searching for reputation" says Titus Brown, a genomics (基因组学) researcher at the University of California, Davis. "To get grants and jobs you have to be relevant and achieve some level of public recognition. Anything you do that advances your presence- especially in a larger sphere, outside the communities you know- is a net win."
paragraphs.translation: 最终，与同事分享数据、软件和材料可以帮助早期职业研究人员获得认可——这是成功的关键组成部分。加州大学戴维斯分校的基因组学研究员Titus Brown说：“你寻找的东西是声誉。”“要获得资助和工作，你必须相关并达到一定程度的公众认可。你所做的任何提升你存在的事——尤其是在你熟悉圈子之外的更大领域——都是净收益。”

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: In the beginning of the movie l, Robot, a robot has to decide whom to save after two cars plunge into the water-Del Spooner or a child. Even though Spooner screams "Save her Save her!" The robot rescues him because it calculates that he has a 45 percent chance of survival compared to Sarah's 11 percent. The robot's decision and its calculated approach raise an important question: would humans make the same choice? And which choice would we want our robotic counterparts to make?
paragraphs.translation: 电影《我，机器人》开头，一个机器人必须在两辆车坠入水中后决定救谁——德尔·斯普纳还是一个孩子。尽管斯普纳尖叫着“救她！救她！”，机器人救了他，因为它计算出他生存的概率为45%，而莎拉的概率为11%。机器人的决策及其计算方式提出了一个重要问题：人类会做出同样的选择吗？我们希望我们的机器人伙伴做出哪种选择？

paragraphs.text: Isaac Asimov evaded the whole notion of morality in devising his three laws of robotics, which hold that 1. Robots cannot harm humans or allow humans to come to harm; 2. Robots must obey humans, except where the order would conflict with law 1; and 3. Robots must act in self-preservation, unless doing so conflicts with laws 1 or 2. These laws are programmed into Asimov's robots-they don't have to think, judge, or value. They don't have to like humans or believe that hurting them is wrong or bad. They simply don't do it.
paragraphs.translation: 艾萨克·阿西莫夫在设计他的机器人三定律时回避了道德的概念，这些定律规定：1. 机器人不得伤害人类或允许人类受到伤害；2. 机器人必须服从人类，除非该命令与第一定律冲突；3. 机器人必须自我保存，除非这样做与第一或第二定律冲突。这些定律被编程进阿西莫夫的机器人中——它们无需思考、判断或评估。它们不需要喜欢人类，也不需要认为伤害人类是错误或糟糕的。它们只是不去做。

paragraphs.text: The robot who rescues Spooner's life in I, Robot follows Asimov's zeroth law: robots cannot harm humanity(as opposed to individual humans) or allow humanity to come to harm--an expansion of the first law that allows robots to determine what's in the greater good. Under the first law, a robot could not harm a dangerous gunman, but under the zeroth law, a robot could kill the gunman to save others.
paragraphs.translation: 在《我，机器人》中救了斯普纳一命的机器人遵循阿西莫夫的第零定律：机器人不得伤害人类整体（相对于个体人类）或允许人类整体受到伤害——这是对第一定律的扩展，允许机器人判断什么对大多数人有利。在第一定律下，机器人不能伤害危险的持枪歹徒，但在第零定律下，机器人可以杀死歹徒来拯救他人。

paragraphs.text: Whether it's possible to program a robot with safeguards such as Asimov's laws is debatable. A word such as "harm" is vague (what about emotional harm? Is replacing a human employ harm?), and abstract concepts present coding problems. The robots in Asimov's fiction expose complications and loopholes in the three laws, and even when the laws work, robots still have to assess the situation.
paragraphs.translation: 是否可以为机器人编程加入如阿西莫夫定律这样的保护措施是值得商榷的。像“伤害”这样的词是模糊的（情感伤害呢？取代人类雇员是伤害吗？），抽象概念带来了编码问题。阿西莫夫小说中的机器人暴露了三定律的复杂性和漏洞，即使定律有效，机器人仍需评估情况。

paragraphs.text: Assessing situations can be complicated. A robot has to identify the players, conditions, and possible outcomes for various scenarios. It's doubtful that a computer program can do that-at least, not without some undesirable results. A roboticist at the Bristol Robotics Laboratory programmed a robot to save human proxies (替身) called "H-bots" from danger.
paragraphs.translation: 评估情况可能很复杂。机器人必须识别参与者、条件和各种可能结果的场景。计算机程序能否做到这一点令人怀疑——至少，没有一些不良结果是不可能的。布里斯托尔机器人实验室的一位机器人学家编程让机器人拯救被称为“H-bots”的人类替身免受危险。

paragraphs.text: When one H-bot headed for danger, the robot successfully pushed it out of the way. But when two H-bots became imperiled, the robot choked 42 percent of the time, unable to decide which to save and letting them both "die. "The experiment highlights the importance of morality: without it, how can a robot decide whom to save or what's best for humanity, especially if it can't calculate survival odds?
paragraphs.translation: 当一个H-bot走向危险时，机器人成功将其推开。但当两个H-bot陷入危险时，机器人有42%的时间会卡住，无法决定救哪个，导致两者都“死亡”。该实验突显了道德的重要性：没有道德，机器人如何决定救谁或什么对人类最有利，尤其是当它无法计算生存概率时？

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: Our world now moves so fast that we seldom stop to see just how far we have come in just a few years. The latest iPhone 6s, for example, has a dual-core processor and fits nicely into your pocket. By comparison, you would expect to find a technological specification like this on your standard laptop in an office anywhere in the world.
paragraphs.translation: 我们的世界如今发展如此之快，以至于我们很少停下来审视仅在短短几年内我们取得了多大进展。例如，最新的iPhone 6s拥有双核处理器，并且能轻松放入口袋。相比之下，你可能会在世界任何地方办公室的标准笔记本电脑上找到类似的技术规格。

paragraphs.text: It's no wonder what new applications for the Internet of Things are moving ahead fast when almost every new device we buy has a plug on the end of it or a wireless connection to the internet. Soon, our current smartphone lifestyle will expand to create our own smart home lifestyle too.
paragraphs.translation: 难怪物联网的新应用发展迅速，因为我们购买的几乎每一个新设备都配有插头或无线网络连接。很快，我们当前的智能手机生活方式将扩展，创造出我们自己的智能家居生活方式。

paragraphs.text: All researches agree that close to 25 billion devices, things and sensors will be connected by 2020 which incidentally is also the moment that Millennials (千禧一代) are expected to make up 75 percent of our overall workforce, and the fully connected home. become a reality for large numbers of people worldwide.
paragraphs.translation: 所有研究都同意，到2020年，接近250亿设备、物品和传感器将被连接，这恰好也是千禧一代预计占我们整体劳动力75%的时刻，而全连接的家将成为全球许多人的现实。

paragraphs.text: However, this is just the tip of the proverbial iceberg as smart buildings and even cities increasingly become the norm as leaders and business owners begin to wake up to the massive savings that technology can deliver through connected sensors and new forms of automation coupled with intelligent energy and facilities management.
paragraphs.translation: 然而，这只是众所周知的冰山一角，因为智能建筑甚至城市正日益成为常态，领导者和企业主开始意识到技术通过连接传感器和新形式的自动化，结合智能能源和设施管理，所能带来的巨大节省。

paragraphs.text: Online security cameras, intelligent lighting and a wealth of sensors that control both temperature and air quality are offering an unprecedented level of control, efficiency, and improvements to what were once classed necessary costs when running a business or managing a large building.
paragraphs.translation: 在线安全摄像头、智能照明以及大量控制温度和空气质量的传感器，正在为运营企业或管理大型建筑时曾被视为必要成本提供前所未有的控制水平、效率和改进。

paragraphs.text: We can expect that the ever-growing list of devices, systems and environments remain connected, always online and talking to each other. The big benefit will not only be in the housing of this enormous and rapidly growing amount of data, but will also be in the ability to run real time data analytics to extract actionable and ongoing knowledge.
paragraphs.translation: 我们可以预期，不断增长的设备、系统和环境列表将保持连接，始终在线并相互交流。巨大的好处不仅在于存储这些庞大且快速增长的数据，还在于运行实时数据分析以提取可操作和持续知识的能力。

paragraphs.text: The biggest and most exciting challenge of this technology is how to creatively leverage this ever-growing amount of data to deliver cost savings, improvements and tangible benefits to both businesses and citizens of these smart cities.
paragraphs.translation: 这项技术最大、最令人兴奋的挑战是如何创造性地利用这些不断增长的数据，为这些智慧城市的商业和市民带来成本节约、改进和切实利益。

paragraphs.text: The good news is that most of this technology is already invented. Let's face it, it wasn't too long ago that the idea of working from anywhere and at any time was some form of a distant utopian (乌托邦式的) dream, and yet now we can perform almost any office-based task from any location in the world as long as we have access to the internet.
paragraphs.translation: 好消息是，这项技术的大部分已经发明。让我们面对现实，不久前，在任何地点任何时间工作的想法还是一种遥远的乌托邦式梦想，但现在，只要我们能接入互联网，我们就能在世界任何地方执行几乎任何办公室任务。

paragraphs.text: It's time to wake up to the fact that making smart buildings, cities and homes will dramatically improve our quality of life in the years ahead.
paragraphs.translation: 是时候意识到，建设智能建筑、城市和家园将在未来几年显著提高我们的生活质量。

questionGroups.sourceText: 青海湖位于海拔 3,205米、青海省省会西宁以西约 100公里处,是中国最大的咸水湖,面积 4,317平方公里,最深处25.5米,有 23条河注入湖中,其中大部分是季节性的。百分之八十的湖水源于五条主要河流。青海湖位于跨越亚洲的几条候鸟迁徙路线的交叉处。许多鸟类把青海湖作为迁徙过程中的暂息地。湖的西侧是著名的"鸟岛",吸引着来自世界各地的观鸟者。每年夏天，游客们也来这里观看国际自行车比赛。

answer.modelTranslation: Qinghai Lake, situated at an altitude of 3,205 meters and about 100 kilometers west of Xining, the capital of Qinghai Province, is the largest saltwater lake in China, covering an area of 4,317 square kilometers with a maximum depth of 25.5 meters. Twenty-three rivers flow into the lake, most of which are seasonal. Eighty percent of the lake's water comes from five main rivers. Qinghai Lake is located at the intersection of several migratory bird routes across Asia. Many birds use Qinghai Lake as a stopover during their migration. The famous 'Bird Island' on the lake's west side attracts birdwatchers from around the world. Every summer, tourists also come here to watch the international bicycle race.
translationNotes: 注意使用过去分词作后置定语，如'situated at an altitude of 3,205 meters'
'位于'可以翻译为'situated at'或'located at'
'以西'翻译为'west of'，表示地理位置
'是中国最大的咸水湖'使用一般现在时，因为这是一个事实性描述
'有23条河注入湖中'中'有'翻译为'flow into'，表示河流汇入湖泊
'其中大部分是季节性的'使用'most of which are seasonal'作为非限制性定语从句
'百分之八十的湖水源于五条主要河流'中'源于'翻译为'comes from'
'位于跨越亚洲的几条候鸟迁徙路线的交叉处'中'跨越亚洲'翻译为'across Asia'，表示地理位置的跨越
'许多鸟类把青海湖作为迁徙过程中的暂息地'中'把...作为'翻译为'use...as'，表示用途
'吸引着来自世界各地的观鸟者'中'吸引着'翻译为'attracts'，表示吸引力
